the extent of DNA structural change caused by silver ions was different in methylated DNA and non-methylized DNA, and the extent of DNA perturbation by silver ion was sequence dependent.
silver ions can be used to enhance the fluorescence of DNA intercalating dyes, which can be used as an indicator for the presence of methylated DNA.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

silver ions could enhance the interaction of DNA with intercalating molecules, and the extent of DNA structural alteration by silver ions could be used to distinguish between methylated and un-methylated DNA in the case of GC rich DNA.
the intercalating molecules could discriminate methylated and nonmethylated DNA, and silver ions could enhance their discrimination ability.
the intercalating molecules could be used as a detection tool for DNA methylation in a simple and cost-effective manner.

the extent of DNA structural alteration by silver ions is dependent on the sequence of the DNA molecule.
